title: Venus' Kiss
notes: Detective-cast (Conan, Kogoro, Ran, Inspector Megure, Officer Takagi) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved (person/location/object). The old wiki-derived case file (cases/ep169_venus_kiss.json) named Murakawa as the culprit and this holds up against the full transcript -- no correction to label.murderer_id was needed. However the old file was much thinner: it had a single generic 'Beika Street Aquarium' location instead of the distinct control room / make-up room / backstage corridor / shell tank / locker room the plot actually depends on, no backstory persons for Murakawa's dead wife and child or for Michiko's father (the President of Oosawa Construction, whose visit to the aquarium is what let Murakawa overhear Michiko mocking him), only one generic 'knows' edge type where the transcript supports specific verbs (assaults, drags_body_of, stages_alibi_using, drowns, mocks), and it flattened three genuinely comparative pieces of evidence (the single-spot foundation smear vs. her scraped cheek, the working emergency-drain test vs. her drowning without pressing it, and the upside-down fresh lipstick mark vs. the washed-out trace on his locker-room shirt) into two generic physical clues without the comparison that makes them work as clues. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The foundation smear on the shell mechanism floor was found in exactly one spot, matching the scraped patch of foundation on Oosawa's cheek -- a natural drowning struggle would smear make-up across multiple spots, so a single spot proves her face was deliberately held down against the floor.

A live test-run proved the shell's internal emergency drain switch works perfectly; for a professional performer who could hold her breath underwater for 4 minutes, drowning without ever pressing a working escape button is inconsistent with an accident.

A fresh, upside-down lipstick mark matching Oosawa's lipstick was found on Murakawa's neck/upper back -- a position and orientation only explainable by having carried her unconscious body over his shoulder -- and a second, partially washed-out trace of the same mark was found on his spare sweatshirt in the locker room, showing he had tried to launder away an earlier instance of the same evidence.

edges.detail: laughed dismissively while talking with her father, unaware Murakawa was overhearing, about not being caught for the hit-and-run
Minegishi performs the show's first slot
leaves the control room under the pretext of going to the restroom
knocks Oosawa unconscious while she is applying her make-up
places the medicine wrap on her leg to misdirect the cause of death
carries her unconscious body over his shoulder through the corridor to the shell hatch
returns to the control room as if nothing happened
